belief: Winning is everything, and losing means I'm nothing.
origins: Sports, school, business, and even church ministries can teach that only winners matter. Parents who cheer wins and sulk over losses, coaches who shame mistakes, and a culture that celebrates champions make losing feel like disgrace. Fear of losing can make us avoid trying.
teaches: Paul uses the race as a picture: “Run in such a way as to take the prize,” and at the end of his life, “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” Notice he does not say, “I won every race.” Solomon observes, “The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong… For time and chance happen to all.” Paul says, “In all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.” The psalmist says, “It is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another.” Faithfulness, not victory, is the measure God gives.
self_statements: If I lose, I am a loser.
I have to win to be valued.
Winners matter and losers do not.
I would rather not try than lose.
errors: Seeing outcomes as win or total loss.
questions: Where did I learn that only winning counts?
What have I learned from my losses?
Who do I admire, and is it for winning or for character?
What does faithfulness look like in my situation?
What would I attempt if losing were not a disaster?
What does God say about worth apart from outcomes?
truth: My worth does not depend on winning. Faithfulness, effort, and character matter most, and God sees them. I can compete with joy, lose with grace, and be more than a conqueror through Christ’s love.
hw_truths: I can finish the race and keep the faith.
Time and chance happen to all.
I am more than a conqueror through Christ.
log: Each week, note one effort made and one lesson from a loss.
actions: Write who taught you that only winning counts.
Write three lessons from a recent loss.
Do something you might not win.
Cheer for someone who tried and lost.
prayer: Lord, I fear losing. Teach me that faithfulness matters more than winning, and help me compete with joy and lose with grace, knowing Your love does not change. Amen.
hw_questions: Who taught me only wins count?
What have I learned from losing?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can finish the race and keep the faith, win or lose.”
